## Historical audit: S0031

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_184317253/trajectory.jsonl`. This audit covers only supplied chunk 2 of 3; image pixels and other chunks are not visible.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, JSONL line 13, [0,189257) | The explicit goal was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph with separate geometry and a matching camera, without using the reference as a texture. The student’s code interprets it as a historic tiled chamber; that semantic interpretation is not independently verified. |
| Line 13, prior student programs and runner feedback | Two complete builds model multiple objects: walls, dome, fireplace, cabinets, door, cauldron, vessels and barrier. They define ceramic colors, procedural plaster noise and bump, iron and wood materials. Rims, handles, feet, cabinet pieces and supports are separate positioned components; actual contact or connection is not verified. No human pose is modeled. |
| Lines 13 and 15, student programs | After step 2 feedback, the student revised the camera from `(-3.30,-.60,1.50)`, lens 24.5, to `(-2.50,-3.20,1.65)`, lens 29; moved the cauldron and barrier; enlarged the dome; made tiles denser; and reduced lighting and exposure. These are observed adjustments, not evidence that camera, pose, lighting, occlusion or framing improved. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 14, [0,3801); `model_response`, line 15, [0,15230) | The fresh, read-only session was supplied the reference and two render images and returned a complete third program. It recorded zero tool calls. The sequence demonstrates iterative autonomous revision after runner feedback, but does not expose the student’s visual diagnosis or prove what it perceived. |
| `execute`, line 16, [0,15865); `execution_result`, line 17, [0,111703); `select`, line 18, [0,59) | Step 3 actually ran. The runner reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and selected step 3. Its log reports 16 render samples despite 64 requested in the program. Execution success is not visual or geometric correctness. |

**Teacher input:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt is visible in this chunk. Consequently there is no evidence of adoption of teacher advice; the runner’s comparison request is feedback, not a teacher diagnosis.

**Outcome and lessons:** The observed outcome is a successful build/render and selection, with overall reconstruction correctness **unknown**—not a verified formal success or an algorithm failure. There is no empty patch or visible technical interruption. A transferable process observation is that full-scene revisions can follow rendered feedback while separately changing camera, geometry and illumination; the specific tile spacing, cauldron placement and exposure are task-specific choices. Whether any revision improved resemblance, whether parts truly connect, and whether render brightness or framing is correct remain unresolved hypotheses because neither the reference nor renders are visible to this audit.
